issues.legal_issue: An alternative defence may be added to a written statement when it is relevant to a live issue, does not contradict the existing defence or withdraw an admission, and any resulting prejudice or delay can be addressed by costs.
material_facts: The defendant had pleaded that he was a lessee, not a licensee.
During trial, he sought to add an alternative plea that, if found to be a licensee, he was entitled to an irrevocable licence because he had carried out permanent works and incurred expenses.

The court found that the proposed plea was neither inconsistent with nor repugnant to the existing defence, and that it responded to the issue of whether he could be dispossessed if found to be a licensee.
The court rejected the finding that the amendment withdrew an admission or would cause irretrievable prejudice.
The amendment application had been made after prolonged delay, but the plaintiff could be compensated by costs.
The plaintiff asserted that licence fees remained unpaid, and the court required payment of arrears as a condition of allowing the amendment.
issues.conclusion: The defendant could amend the written statement to add only the alternative plea of entitlement to the benefit of Section 60(b) of the Indian Easements Act, subject to paying the outstanding licence fees and costs.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, amendment of pleadings is discretionary and should generally be allowed when necessary to determine the real controversy, including an alternative defence in a written statement, unless it introduces a new cause of action or case, contradicts admitted facts, withdraws an admission, causes prejudice that cannot be compensated, or defeats a right accrued through lapse of time. Delay may be compensated by costs. The court relied on A.K. Gupta & Sons v. Damodar Valley Corporation, Smt. Ganga Bai v. Vijay Kumar, and M/s. Ganesh Trading Company v. Moji Ram. The proposed defence invoked Section 60(b) of the Indian Easements Act, 1882.

rule.if: written_statement_amendment_proceeding and alternative_defence_proposed and amendment_relevant_to_live_issue and amendment_not_inconsistent_with_existing_defence and no_admission_withdrawn and prejudice_compensable_by_costs and delay_compensable_by_costs and outstanding_fees_asserted

predicates.written_statement_amendment_proceeding: A defendant sought to amend a written statement during the proceeding.
predicates.alternative_defence_proposed: The defendant proposed a defence that would apply if the court rejected the defendant’s primary position.
predicates.amendment_relevant_to_live_issue: The proposed defence addressed an issue already arising for determination in the proceeding.
predicates.amendment_not_inconsistent_with_existing: The proposed defence could be advanced alongside the defence already pleaded without contradicting it.
predicates.no_admission_withdrawn: The proposed amendment did not withdraw an admission made in the existing pleading.
predicates.prejudice_compensable_by_costs: Any prejudice to the opposing party from the amendment could be compensated by costs.
predicates.delay_compensable_by_costs: The delay in seeking the amendment could be addressed by an award of costs.
predicates.outstanding_fees_asserted: The opposing party asserted that fees remained unpaid.

issues.definition: When a defendant seeks to add a relevant alternative defence to a written statement without inconsistency or withdrawal of an admission, and any prejudice and delay can be addressed by costs, the amendment may be permitted subject to payment of asserted outstanding fees and costs.
